input: This passage describes the sizing basis for a gravity settler that is used to remove activated sludge from a process stream. The design is based on an overflow rate of 1.74 m h-1 at a throughput of 194 m3 h-1, giving a plan area of 111 m2. In other words, the size of the settler follows directly from the combination of the throughput that has to be handled and the overflow rate that has been adopted for design purposes. It is nevertheless important to note the basis on which the overflow rate has been selected. The overflow-rate basis is a vendor rule for this solid, and no settling test on the actual slurry has been run. This means that the plan area, while it follows clearly from the stated design figures, ultimately rests on a general rule supplied for the solid rather than on settling behaviour measured directly for the slurry that the settler will treat in practice. Overall, the sizing is therefore best understood as a rule-based design figure, with the absence of an actual settling test representing an important limitation on the extent to which the design has been verified. The passage therefore separates the sizing calculation itself from the separate question of how firmly the governing design rate has been established for the material in question.
target: A gravity settler removing activated sludge from a process stream is sized on a design overflow rate of 1.74 m h-1. At a throughput of 194 m3 h-1, the overflow rate gives a plan area of 111 m2. The area follows directly from the throughput and the adopted overflow rate: the settler must present enough plan area for the flow to pass at or below that rate. The overflow-rate basis is a vendor rule for this solid. No settling test on the actual slurry has been run. The design therefore rests on a general rule for the solid, not on measured settling behaviour of the slurry to be treated. That distinction fixes the status of the plan area. The arithmetic of the sizing is complete on the stated figures, but the input that governs the answer has not been checked against the actual material. A settling test on the slurry would test the overflow rate itself; until it is run, the area is a rule-based design value. The settler sizing is consequently complete as a calculation and incomplete as a verification. The plan area is the answer to the stated throughput at the adopted rate. The open point is not the division that produces the area but the rate that the division takes as given, and that point can only be closed by settling behaviour measured on the slurry itself.
